html:
#ADR-049: SWIM Partition-Heal Rejoin + Asynchronous Indirect-Ping Relay

#Status

Accepted and merged (2026-10-22) into include/quark/core/cluster.hpp, with the merge conditions in "Decision" below met; see "Merge record" at the end. This ADR resolves OpenQuestions.md item 021 (the two SWIM defects found 2026-10-21).

#Question

SwimMembership (021 §3, include/quark/core/cluster.hpp) has two defects that run_swim_chaos.sh measured on 5 real processes in separate network namespaces with iptables cuts:

  1. Partition-heal collapse. apply_update lets Dead replace Alive at an equal incarnation, and Dead is terminal. After a heal, the node that was cut off gossips its stale "everyone is Dead" view, and healthy nodes believe it about each other before the subject can refute. Measured: isolating node 5 for 10 s left node 1 at *DDDD, and a {1,2}|{3,4,5} split left only the 4–5 pair connected. Also, Join on a node that is already Dead does nothing, so a healed node can never get back in. This contradicts 021 §1.
  2. The indirect ping does not work over a real transport. The PingReq relay expects the subject's Ack to arrive in the same call stack, which only the loopback does. Over TcpTransport the Ack is dropped. Measured: with only the 1↔2 link cut, incarnation went from 1 to 31 in 22 s.

The question is how to fix both together without breaking any of the following: the single-thread contract, determinism under the injected clock, crash detection, the rule that a departed or re-epoched node is not resurrected, the accidental-merge guard, bounded state, and the existing tests.

#Designs (one-line summaries)

  1. SAR/ART: Subject-Authoritative Resurrection + Bounded Async Relay Table. Only a frame from the subject itself, or a Join from the subject, can lift its tombstone. A third-party Dead at an equal incarnation becomes Suspect, but only if this node heard the subject directly within suspicion_timeout. Tombstones are probed one per tombstone_probe_interval. leave() sets a sticky departed bit, carried in bit 7 of the wire status. The relay keeps an inline std::array<RelaySlot,32> with tagged sequence numbers and deadlines on the injected clock.
  2. FHT/TR: Expiring first-hand tombstones + accusation-targeted digest + stateless token relay (revised). A node adopts Dead only from its own suspicion timer. A Dead learned from gossip is downgraded to Suspect and then checked with a direct verify ping (R1b). The digest puts the receiver's entry first, then the sender's self entry, then piggybacked changes, then a rotating cursor (R4'). Tombstones expire and are probed within a budget (R5'). Left is written at inc + 2^32 and only a Join from the subject lifts it (R6'). The relay keeps no state: the requester id and a splitmix token travel inside the Ping and its Ack.
  3. Lifeguard-SWIM. Dead is a local opinion that requires this node's own failed probe. Join assigns the rejoining node's incarnation at the seed. The relay is a 16-slot table keyed per requester and answers with a PingReqNack. A Local Health Multiplier (LHM) stretches the timeouts of a node that looks isolated. Reprobes and Config::seeds drive rejoin.

#Evidence table

A claim counts only if it survived red-teaming in its rebutted form and was proven CORRECT by executed C++. That C++ was built with g++ 15.2 and clang++ 21.1 on Linux bare metal, under ASan+UBSan and TSan. Each prover first reproduced both defects on HEAD ed4c19f, using a deterministic deferred-delivery fabric that never delivers in the sender's call stack.

#Decision

Winner: Design 2, FHT/TR (expiring first-hand tombstones + accusation-targeted digest + stateless token relay), in its revised form (R1b, R4', R5', R6', admit() through the Join rule, wire-status range check, indirect_ns() clamp).

Rationale, following the ranking rules:

  1. Safety gate. Design 3 fails it. Its safe claim S3 is WRONG: under correlated failure the LHM saturates on healthy nodes because dead relays send no response. That stretches crash detection to 1236 rounds and lets erased entries come back from stale gossip, with 2766 phantom node-rounds. No cheap fix was stated, because the stretch is the LHM mechanism itself. It also bends a required invariant: a crashed node must be detected within ack + indirect + suspicion. Its S1 failure comes from a real but pre-existing TcpTransport race (see residual risks). Designs 1 and 2 have no safe claim marked WRONG.
  2. Proven beats claimed. Design 2 has 13 proven and 2 disproven; Design 1 has 11 proven and 2 disproven. More important is what was disproven. Both of Design 2's failures are fast-claim sub-clauses: sizeof +32 B, and the digest coverage gap during bursts. In both cases the behavioural property (accusation-first, zero relay state) was proven. Design 1's failure is a correctness bound. With a realistic graveyard of 40 tombstones, the {1,2}|{3,4,5} heal took 121–139 ticks (≈16.7 s) instead of 40, because round-robin probing at one tombstone per second starves the cross-split probe. Its F2 failure follows from that.
  3. Measured protocol cost (the task defines "fast" as bounded convergence, bounded false positives and bounded state). Design 2 heals faster in every shared scenario: isolate 600 ms vs 1.2 s, split 480 ms vs 1.3 s, graveyard 1.08 s vs 16.7 s. It is the only design proven at n=64, with 0 false Dead, and the ablations show its R1b/R4' revisions are load-bearing. It has 0 Dead over 320k periods at p=5% loss (Design 1 was tested only at p=1%). It adds 0 B of relay state, against 1536 B, and its sizeof is 784 B against 2344 B. Crash detection matches HEAD in both. Design 1 is better on CPU per frame (+2.5–3.5% vs +18% at n=5 and +65% at n=64 cap 8). This is control-plane cost (5 frames per node-tick in all builds), not the message hot path, and it has a cheap fix (condition 2 below).
  4. Core invariants. Design 2 adds no atomics, no thread-visible state and no relay table. It keeps view()/epoch() as the mutex-published immutable snapshot and reads only now_ns(). Actor-level invariants (single executor, FIFO, stable placement) are untouched.

Conditions before merge (all cheap, all within the winning design):

  1. Fix the F2 burst starvation. Reserve at least ceil((max_gossip_updates-2)/2) slots per frame for the rotating cursor, so piggybacked changes cannot take every slot. Re-run the accuse and coverage experiments, and require the coverage gap to stay within ceil(|members|/reserved) during bursts too.
  2. Remove the O(n log n) sort from every frame. Build the cursor's sorted id vector only when republish() or a tombstone transition changes the roster, reusing its capacity. Re-run the per-frame bench and require n=64 cap 8 to be within +25% of HEAD.
  3. tests/netem/run_swim_chaos.sh acceptance gate. Design 2 was proven only on a 3-node in-process TcpTransport rig. Design 1 ran the full 5-process network-namespace rig. All five scenarios (form, isolate, asym, split, flaky) must end all-alive on the patched swim_chaos_node. This is the single tie-breaking experiment if this decision is challenged: run both Design 1 (with a 500 ms probe interval) and Design 2 on that rig, with a 40-tombstone graveyard pre-seeded.
  4. Add the MemberStatus::Left case to tests/netem/swim_chaos_node.cpp:80 (-Wswitch).
  5. Land the prover harness (DeferredFabric with drop, hold, seeded shuffle and per-wave clock advance) and the HEAD-failing scenarios as tests/cluster_swim_*_test.cpp. Restate F1 (sizeof +32 B, from the new Config fields) and F4 (q^k ≈ 3.4e-2 at p=5%) correctly in the test comments.

Design 1 also contributed one finding the merge should keep: its real-rig evidence that subject-origin frames plus a target-first digest heal TCP clusters in under 1 s. Design 2's R4 already covers the target-first digest.

#Residual risks

  • Resurrection after tombstone expiry or cap eviction. C5 holds only while the tombstone is resident. A peer partitioned for longer than tombstone_ttl_ns (default 60 s) that holds a stale Alive can re-admit an erased node until it is detected again. tombstone_ttl_ns must be larger than the longest partition the deployment tolerates. This is an operational constraint; assert it at startup against 2*(ack+indirect+suspicion).
  • Mixed-version wire. Wire status 3 (Left) is new, and the relay echoes subject and subject_incarnation in Ack. An old node treats Left as live, and an old subject leaves the relay inert. A rolling upgrade across this change needs a SWIM wire-version gate or a flag day. None of the three designs claimed mixed-version compatibility.
  • Left band. Every leave/rejoin cycle adds 2^32 to the incarnation, so u64 allows about 2^32 cycles per identity. That is safe, but visible in metrics (009).
  • Join, Left and resurrection trust m.from. Without SecureTransport (020, ADR-040), a spoofed Join with subject == from re-admits a departed id. This is no weaker than HEAD.
  • Relay RTT budget. The 4-hop relay chain must complete within the tick-quantized indirect window. The measured threshold is 4d < ceil(indirect_ns/T)*T. On a WAN, raise indirect_timeout_ns.
  • Probe-backs to dead addresses. At most B=2 per tick, sent until TTL. Over TcpTransport these cause dial and backoff churn and grow the per-peer outq_. That queue growth is already a 022 concern (see ADR-046's PeerBacklog finding) and is outside SwimMembership's scope.
  • Pre-existing TcpTransport fd race. close_fd() runs before io_.del_fd() at tcp_transport.hpp:517-519 and :625-626, which races epoll_ctl against accept4 fd reuse. It was found by Design 3's prover and HEAD reproduces it (1/10). It is not part of this ADR, but it must be fixed and tracked separately (OpenQuestions 010/021).
  • Slower cluster-wide Dead in theory. Because Dead is re-derived first-hand plus a verify ping, convergence can take up to one extra suspicion_timeout on nodes other than the detector. This was not observed: worst 1188 ms, identical to HEAD.
  • Determinism is per toolchain, because unordered_map iteration order is part of the trace. The g++ and clang++ traces matched only because both used libstdc++.

#Spec recommendations

  • 021-Cluster-Formation-and-Lifecycle.md
    • §1 "Cluster identity": state the semantics that make "a node rejoining after a partition can tell stale from current" true. Dead is first-hand only. A Dead learned from gossip is a Suspect hint, checked by a verify ping. A tombstone is lifted only by an Alive or Suspect at a strictly higher incarnation, or by a Join where subject == from, which re-admits at max(presented, tomb.inc+1). The seed returns the assigned incarnation in JoinAck.
    • §3: add a subsection "SWIM failure-detector rules (ADR-049)" listing R1/R1b/R2/R3/R4'/R5'/R6'/R7, the stateless token relay, and the new Config fields: indirect_timeout_ns (0 = ack), tombstone_ttl_ns=60 s, max_tombstones, tombstone_probe_interval_ns, verify_ping_budget, and the probe-back budget B.
    • §3 "Scale down": graceful leave writes authoritative Left@inc+2^32. Self-leave is never refuted. Only the subject's own Join re-admits.
    • §3 "Rolling upgrade": the SWIM wire format changes (status 3, relay echo fields). Mark this change as outside the back-compat window and require a version gate.
    • Open questions: add "tombstone TTL vs longest tolerated partition".
  • 010-Distribution.md, "Membership": the published view is the non-tombstone set (Alive/Suspect). Dead is adopted only from a node's own suspicion timer; Left is a separate authoritative departure. Indirect ping is asynchronous, with correlation carried in the frame and no relay state. Add a note that the relay round trip is 4 hops and must fit within indirect_timeout_ns. Cite ADR-049 under Status.
  • 014-Testing-Model.md, "Fault injection": require a deferred-delivery transport for any protocol test whose correctness depends on reply timing. It never delivers in the sender's call stack, and supports delivery in waves, seeded reorder, per-directed-link drop, a hold mode that queues frames and releases them FIFO at heal (modelling TcpTransport's outq_), and a per-wave clock advance for latency. Add the rule that a defect fix must first reproduce the defect on HEAD. Name tests/netem/run_swim_chaos.sh as the multi-process acceptance tier for membership changes.
  • 018-Clocks-and-Deadlines.md: every SWIM timer (suspicion, indirect window, relay-token bucket now/indirect_ns, tombstone TTL, probe-back spacing, verify-ping pacing) uses the injectable monotonic clock, never wall time. Detection and heal bounds are stated tick-quantized, with each stage rounded up to the tick (proven: 840 ms against a 700 ms un-quantized bound, identical on HEAD). Rule 2a: only Acks to the node's own probes feed the smoothed RTT. Relayed and probe-back round trips must not.
  • OpenQuestions.md, item 021: mark it resolved in mechanism by ADR-049, pending merge under the conditions above. Add the TcpTransport close_fd/del_fd race as a separate 010/021 entry.

#Merge record (2026-10-22)

Merged into include/quark/core/cluster.hpp from the Design 2 prover's patch, re-applied onto the existing file. The existing doc comments were kept, and the prover-only scaffolding was dropped (QUARK_SWIM_PATCH marker, the piggyback_digest ablation switch, extra diagnostic accessors). All evidence below is from thnak-server: bare-metal Ubuntu 26.04, 28 cores, g++ 15.2, clang++ 21.1.

ConditionHow it was metEvidence

2. No per-frame sortcursor walks a cached sorted_ids_, rebuilt only on add/erase; piggyback passes are skipped when tx_pending_ == 0per-frame cost vs old code: n=64 cap 8 +17% (2004 vs 1713 ns; limit +25%; the prover's patch was +59%); n=5 +16%
3. run_swim_chaos.shall 5 scenarios on 5 processes, one per network namespaceall end all-alive; isolate heals ≈0.9 s and split ≈1.0 s after the cut lifts; asym: 0 Suspect samples, incarnation stays 1 (was 31)
4. -Wswitch in swim_chaos_nodeLeft case addedclean build
5. Harness + failing-on-old-code teststests/swim_deferred_fabric.hpp, cluster_swim_partition_heal_test, cluster_swim_async_relay_testold code: heal test fails 32/32 heal runs, relay test 363 bumps. New code: worst heal 600 ms, rejoin 120 ms, crash still detected cluster-wide in 1.08 s, 0 bumps

Full suites on the merged code: g++ 210/210, clang++ 210/210, ASan+UBSan 209/210, TSan 192/193. Both failures are pre-existing test weaknesses, unrelated to SWIM and recorded in OpenQuestions.md:

  • topic_no_quiesce_control (ASan negative control): its race fired in only 1/20 runs on this host.
  • tcp_transport_control_priority_test under TSan: the ordering threshold is missed in 4/10 runs on the old code and 6–7/10 on the new. It is not a data race; the test does not use SwimMembership.
